subject: Recap: ThirdWave migration requirements & shortlist
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Tanaka <sam.tanaka@thirdwave.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@thirdwave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: ThirdWave migration requirements & shortlist

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on constraints. Below is a short recap so we have alignment and a proposed next-step plan. Please flag anything I misrepresented.

Key pain points you reiterated
- Token spend growth on OpenAI chat completions (main product: prompt+retrieval) — currently ~1.2M tokens/day and increasing.
- Latency spikes during peak loads causing user-visible timeouts on mobile.
- Vendor lock concerns: procurement wants exit options from proprietary LLM APIs for licensing and cost predictability.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Front end: React Native; backend: Go microservices on AWS ECS Fargate.
- Model calls today: OpenAI (gpt-4o-ish calls) for assistant + Anthropic Claude for summarization in a few flows.
- Caching: homegrown prefix cache in Redis (no KV-cache reuse across tokens).
- Auth & data flow: API keys stored in Secrets Manager; PII redaction done client-side.

Success criteria for migration / PoC
- Cost per 1k effective tokens reduced by >= 40% (baseline: current blended cost).
- 95th percentile latency for 1–2k RPS sustained traffic <= 350ms for generation endpoint.
- Output fidelity: automated eval pass-rate >= 92% on your top-10 prompts (we'll need those).
- Smooth fall-back: identical public API surface for devs (no changes to the majority of client SDK calls).

Compatibility & constraints you called out
- Must preserve function/tool-calling semantics for a subset of flows (structured JSON outputs).
- A memory/short-term context footprint of frequently used embeddings + retrieval (your retrieval window: ~6k tokens).
- Compliance: logs retained for 90 days; no model-hosted customer PII beyond request time.

Initial model shortlist (quick, subject to eval)
- Llama-3 70B (quantized profile) — good baseline for generation quality.
- Mistral-Instant family (smaller latency-focused variant) — promising for cost/latency trade-offs.
- RedPajama-3 / Orca derivatives (optimize for structured output).

Proposed next steps (short timeline)
1) You: share the top-10 prompt set + 48h of representative logs (anonymized) — Alyssa to confirm. (Target: Tue 2/24)
2) Redwood: send a short PoC scope + eval plan and cost-estimate (I attached a draft eval plan). (Target: Wed 2/25)
3) Tech sync: 60m call with your eng + infra to validate network and runtime constraints (we propose Wed 3/3).
4) Security paperwork: standard NDA + initial security questionnaire (we can start this in parallel).

Attachments included
- thirdwave-current-stack.pdf (your diagram from the call)
- redwood-eval-plan.xlsx (initial metrics & sample evaluation tasks)
- network-reqs.txt (lightweight checklist for VPC/on-prem options)

If that looks right, I'll convert the eval plan to a scoped SOW and schedule the tech sync. Thanks again — happy to be your partner on a low-risk exit path.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
From: Sam Tanaka <sam.tanaka@thirdwave.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@thirdwave.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: ThirdWave migration requirements & shortlist

Thanks — nice write-up, Sofia. A couple of small corrections and clarifications:
- Token numbers: 1.2M/day is total tokens billed; effective prompt+response tokens that matter for cost-calcs are ~850k/day.
- Function calling: we use a thin wrapper for function/tool calls; preserving the JSON schema is critical for downstream services.
- Compliance: logs can be redacted and supplied, but we cannot share any PII-containing rows for the PoC.

Action items from our side
- Alyssa: we'll pull the top-10 prompts and a 48h anonymized log export; expected by Tue 2/24 EOD.
- Eng: we'll attend the tech sync on 3/3 but can push to 3/4 if that helps your team's calendar.

Also — curious if Redwood supports a hybrid routing model where we keep critical flows on Anthropic for a short period during the PoC (warm path), and divert the rest to the open-model stack. That will help us avoid risking latency regressions for critical customers.

Sam
Sam Tanaka
Head of Platform Engineering | ThirdWave AI
sam.tanaka@thirdwave.ai

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: ThirdWave migration requirements & shortlist

Appreciate the clarifications, Sam — noted on the 850k/day effective tokens and the function-calling wrapper. A few internal notes and clarifications for the PoC scope: 

1) Hybrid routing — yes, Redwood supports traffic policies by route/model. For the PoC we recommend a split: 20% critical flows stay on Anthropic (warm path) for 2 weeks, the rest move to the open-model variant. This lets you validate fidelity while we tune caching and batch settings.

2) SDK compatibility — our API can surface a drop-in compatibility layer for your wrapper (we'll map your function schema to our structured-output hooks). We will provide a small client shim (node/Go) during the PoC.

3) Eval plan updates — we'll add a fidelity metric specifically for function outputs (schema correctness rate). Please confirm the exact schema for the four critical functions.

4) Security/start paperwork — sending the standard NDA + security questionnaire via DocuSign today. Please note: for on-prem or VPC installs we require the network checklist in network-reqs.txt to be validated by your infra team.

Next steps I will take this morning
- Finalize PoC SOW and attach pricing assumptions (small one-week smoke test + 4-week eval).
- Add the function-output metric to the eval tab in redwood-eval-plan.xlsx.
- Book tech sync for Tue 3/3 11:00 PT (tentative) — will send an invite once you confirm.

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in for the SOW & infra notes. I'll send the DocuSign link in a separate thread.

Best,
Sofia
